learning_outcomes.text: Classify materials in terms of purpose, method, and form in material testing.
Perform tensile tests on metallic materials by understanding the standards and application of tensile tests.
Classify hardness measurement methods of objects according to their working principles and standards.
Distinguish the purposes of using mechanical/destructive material testing methods.
Classify materials in terms of their mechanical behavior and relate the effect of test conditions on material properties.
Classify impact, bending, and torsion tests and distinguish their working principles.
Acquire knowledge about microstructural analyses of metallic materials and the preparation stages of metallographic examination.

syllabus_topics: Destructive testing systems and their purposes
Introduction to the tensile testing machine, tensile testing standards and their importance
Data to be obtained from tensile testing and strength-deformation calculations
Converting data obtained from tensile tests into graphs
Bending and folding tests of metallic materials
Hardness measurement tests (Brinell, Rockwell, Vickers, Microhardness, Shore A and Shore D hardness measurement methods)
Metallographic examination preparation and microstructure investigations
assessment_rules: The midterm exam accounts for 40% of the grade, and the final exam accounts for 60%. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate decision and specified in the academic calendar.
